sections.h2: Where is Delta County, Colorado, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Delta County sits on Colorado's Western Slope. It covers 1,149 square miles, borders Mesa, Gunnison and Montrose counties, and has Delta as its county seat and largest city, according to Wikipedia.

The legislature created the county on February 11, 1883, out of part of Gunnison County. The name comes from the delta of farmable land where the Uncompahgre River meets the Gunnison River. Orchard City, Cedaredge, Hotchkiss and Paonia are the other communities most owners will name when they describe where a house sits.

Population figures from the Census Bureau show 31,196 people in 2020 and an estimate of 32,178 for July 2025. For a seller, a house in the city of Delta, a farm lot near Hotchkiss and a place in Cedaredge can sit in different tax areas with different mill levies, so the address matters more than the county name.

sections.h2: How is the Delta County economy structured?
sections.html:
Government, agriculture, retail and health services supply the most jobs. A May 2025 economic update from Colorado Mesa University lists 2,779 government jobs, 1,733 agriculture jobs, 1,532 retail jobs and 1,070 health services jobs for 2023.

  • Health care and social assistance had 1,648 average employed in the fourth quarter of 2024, the largest wage total in that report.
  • Public administration averaged 842 employed and retail trade 1,206 in the same quarter.
  • The report put the first quarter 2025 unemployment rate at 6.83 percent, and warns that county estimates for small counties are not highly reliable.

The same report counted 31 foreclosure filings and 7 foreclosure sales in 2024, down from 51 and 17 in 2023.

sections.html:

sections.h2: How do you get around Delta County and reach an airport?
sections.html:
US 50 runs through Delta as Main Street and connects it to Montrose and Grand Junction. State Highway 65 climbs north over Grand Mesa toward I-70, and State Highway 92 starts in Delta and runs east for 73 miles.

Montrose Regional Airport is about 21 miles south of Delta, and Grand Junction, 39 miles north, has scheduled flights and an Amtrak station.

sections.h2: How does Delta County calculate property tax?
sections.html:
Delta County multiplies actual value by an assessment rate, then applies the mill levies of every taxing authority in the property's tax area. The county's property tax explainer walks through each step.

  1. The Assessor classifies the property by its use on January 1.
  2. Residential actual value comes from comparable sales only. For tax years 2025 and 2026 those sales fall between July 1, 2022 and June 30, 2024.
  3. Starting in 2025, residential property has two assessment rates, one for the school district and one for other local governments. The county's 2025 example uses 6.25 percent for local governments and 7.05 percent for schools.
  4. Each taxing authority divides its revenue need by the assessed value inside its boundary to set a mill levy.

The county's worked example uses a $275,000 home and lands at $1,164.61 in total tax. It is an illustration with example levies, so use your own bill for a real number. All of the property tax stays in the county and none funds state services.

sections.h2: What are the Delta County property tax dates?
sections.html:
Taxes are billed for the prior year, and you can pay in full by April 30 or in two halves. The dates below come from the Delta County pages.

ItemDate
Notice of Valuation, real propertyBy May 1
Protest of real property valueBy June 8
First half or full payment optionLast day of February, or April 30 in full
Second halfJune 15
Appeal to County Board of EqualizationBy July 15
Board hearings finishAugust 5
Further appealWithin 30 days of the decision

Real property is revalued in odd-numbered years. Taxes of $25 or less must be paid in full by April 30.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Delta County valuation?
sections.html:
File with the Assessor between January 1 and June 8 by mail, in person or by phone. The county calls an in-person visit the most effective route and advises appealing early.

  • Gather evidence from the Assessor's sales books and neighborhood sales lists.
  • State why the value is wrong and the value you think is right.
  • Expect the Assessor's response by the last working day of June, and a possible property visit to check size and finish.
  • If you disagree, appeal to the County Board of Equalization by July 15. The Board is made up of the county commissioners, and it must notify you of its decision within five working days.

The county page states that prior tax years cannot be appealed through this process, and that the Assessor cannot consider sales after June 30, 2024. Check the current year's page for updated dates.

sections.h2: Who do you call at Delta County for property tax questions?
sections.html:
The Assessor values property and the Treasurer bills and collects. The Assessor's office is at 375 W. 6th St., Delta, phone 970-874-2120, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays, with shorter hours from May 1 through June 8.

The Treasurer is at 501 Palmer Street, Suite 202, Delta, phone 970-874-2135, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. Payments can be made in person there or at the County Annex at 196 W. Hotchkiss Avenue in Hotchkiss, by mail to PO Box 580, Grand Junction, or online through GovPros. The mail page says only a USPS postmark counts as proof.

Recording a deed happens at the Clerk and Recorder, 501 Palmer Street, Suite 211, phone 970-874-2150, where the fee is $43 per document.

sections.h2: What happens if Delta County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax accrues interest at one percent per month, counting part of a month as a full month, under C.R.S. 39-10-104.5. Interest on a missed first half starts March 1, on a missed second half June 16, and on a missed full payment May 1.

Colorado law has a grace window for the first half: if it is paid within 30 days after the treasurer mails the statement, no delinquent interest accrues. Past that, the treasurer can sell the tax lien at the annual sale, and the Delta County pages link rules for that sale. A lien buyer then holds a claim against the house that must be cleared before a clean sale.

A title company asks the Treasurer for a tax certificate before closing, and the county has an online request portal for that. Any unpaid tax comes out of the seller's proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Delta County house with tax due or a deferral?
sections.html:
Yes. Back taxes, interest and any lien payoff are settled at closing from the sale price, so a seller does not need cash up front.

Anyone using Colorado's property tax deferral program should know a sale triggers repayment. The state treasury says the deferral is recorded as a junior lien, and repayment is due 90 days after a sale or a contract of sale, with interest running from May 1 of the year it was claimed. If an owner dies with no surviving spouse, repayment is due one year after death.

If you are selling a Delta County house that needs work, has a tax lien or came through an estate, we can send a written cash offer for the house as it stands.

faqs.q: When is Delta County property tax due?
faqs.a: Taxes can be paid in full by April 30, or in two halves due the last day of February and June 15. Amounts of $25 or less must be paid in full by April 30.

faqs.q: What is the protest deadline for a Delta County property value?
faqs.a: The real property protest deadline is June 8 for the 2026 cycle, by mail, in person or by phone. An appeal to the County Board of Equalization follows by July 15.

faqs.q: What interest does Delta County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: One percent per month under C.R.S. 39-10-104.5, with part of a month counted as a whole month. It starts March 1 for a late first half, June 16 for a late second half and May 1 for a late full payment.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Delta County?
faqs.a: Pay at the Treasurer's office at 501 Palmer Street, Suite 202, Delta, at the County Annex in Hotchkiss, by mail to PO Box 580, Grand Junction, or online through GovPros.

faqs.q: Does selling a house in Delta County end the property tax deferral?
faqs.a: A sale or contract of sale makes the state's deferral repayment due within 90 days. The deferral is a recorded junior lien, so it is paid at or soon after closing.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Delta County?
faqs.a: The Delta County Clerk and Recorder, at 501 Palmer Street, Suite 211, records deeds. The fee listed is $43 per document, plus the state documentary fee when it applies.
